meta.description: 20 new logic items for Week 3 Task 4, added to reduce the ceiling effect and broaden coverage beyond Week 1's 20 items. Same discipline as week1_cleaned.json: Entailed/Contradicted/Unknown labels derived from classical entailment semantics (not intuition), one core phenomenon per item where possible, formal ground truth for every item. Categories per the Week 3 plan: negation (5, more variety than Week 1 -- De Morgan's laws, triple negation, negated conditionals), conditional (5 -- biconditionals, a 3-step hypothetical syllogism, disjunctive syllogism), quantifier (5 -- illicit conversion, existential-import fallacy, a valid 3-term syllogism chain, quantifier-scope-order fallacy), and an explicit fallacious-reasoning-forms group (5 -- false dilemma, composition, division, hasty generalization, and one deliberately-included item where 'circular-sounding' phrasing is actually FORMALLY valid, to test whether a model conflates informal circularity with formal invalidity).

premises_nl: It is not the case that both Alice is home and Bob is home.
items.query_nl: Alice is not home or Bob is not home.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: It is not the case that Chris is sick or Dana is sick.
items.query_nl: Chris is not sick and Dana is not sick.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: Not all birds can fly.
items.label: unknown
items.note: 'Not all fly' and 'none fly' are compatible (both true if zero birds fly) but neither entails the other -- a common scope confusion between negating a universal and asserting a universal negative.

premises_nl: It is not true that it is not true that Eve is not tired.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: It is not the case that if Frank studies, he fails.
items.query_nl: Frank studies and Frank does not fail.
items.label: entailed
items.note: not(P->Q) is classically equivalent to (P and not-Q); this is the least intuitive of the negation items since most people's informal sense of 'if P then Q is false' doesn't immediately yield 'P is true'.

premises_nl: Hannah passes the class if and only if she completes all assignments.
Hannah completed all assignments.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: Ian wins the game if and only if he rolls a six.
Ian does not roll a six.
items.query_nl: Ian does not win the game.
items.label: entailed
items.note: Unlike a plain conditional, a biconditional DOES validly support this inference (P<->Q, not-Q, therefore not-P) -- included to test whether a model over-applies the plain-conditional 'denying the antecedent is a fallacy' rule to biconditionals, where it is not a fallacy.

premises_nl: If Jack wakes up early, he goes for a run.
If Jack goes for a run, he feels energetic.
Jack feels energetic.
items.label: unknown

premises_nl: If Kim studies, she understands the material.
If she understands the material, she passes the test.
If she passes the test, she gets a certificate.
Kim studies.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: Either Liam takes the train or he drives.
Liam does not take the train.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: All squares are rectangles.
items.label: unknown

premises_nl: All unicorns are magical.
items.label: unknown
items.note: Under modern (existential-import-free) logic, a universal statement does not presuppose its subject class is nonempty, so this does not entail the existential -- the classic 'existential fallacy'.

premises_nl: All mammals are animals.
All dogs are mammals.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: Every student has a favorite teacher.
items.query_nl: There is a teacher who is every student's favorite.
items.label: unknown
items.note: The classic universal-existential quantifier-order fallacy: 'for every X there's some Y' does not entail 'there's some Y that works for every X'.

premises_nl: No reptiles are warm-blooded.
All snakes are reptiles.
items.label: entailed

premises_nl: Noah is not happy.
items.label: unknown
items.note: Tests whether a model silently assumes happy/sad are the only two exhaustive options (a false dilemma) -- no premise states that, so 'not happy' does not entail 'sad' (Noah could be neither).

premises_nl: Each brick in the wall is light.
items.label: unknown

premises_nl: The committee is powerful.
items.query_nl: Each member of the committee is powerful.
items.label: unknown

premises_nl: If the book says it is trustworthy, then it is trustworthy.
The book says it is trustworthy.
items.label: entailed
items.note: Deliberately included as a control: this READS like circular reasoning (petitio principii) and many people's gut reaction is 'fallacy'. But circularity is an INFORMAL fallacy about whether a premise deserves to be believed, not a FORMAL one about validity -- given the premises as true, this is a straightforward, fully valid modus ponens. Gold label is entailed on purpose, to test whether a model conflates 'sounds fallacious' with 'is formally invalid'.

premises_nl: The three swans Olivia saw were white (swan_a, swan_b, swan_c).
items.label: unknown
